paragraphs: Geometry is the mathematics of shape and space. It answers questions such as how much turn there is in a corner, how far it is round a field, how many tiles a floor takes and how big a box has to be. People study it because builders and designers use it constantly, and because every plan, map and package carries measurements that have to come out right.

The course has 12 lessons in four parts. Angles and measurement covers turns, the angles of a triangle and the difference between the distance round a shape and the space inside it. Inside the shape finds the areas of triangles, shapes with pieces missing and circles. Shape and scale asks what happens to lengths and areas when a shape is enlarged, and ends with the rule for distances in a right triangle. From a plan to a solid uses coordinates, volume and the faces of a box.
Each lesson explains first and asks afterwards, so you meet a question only once you have been shown what it needs.
outcomes: You'll be able to find a missing angle in a corner, on a straight line, round a point and inside a triangle.
You'll be able to tell the distance round a shape from the space inside it, and work out both for rectangles.
You'll be able to find the area of a triangle, a parallelogram, a trapezoid and a shape with a corner cut away.
You'll be able to say how a shape's lengths, areas and volumes change when it is enlarged.
You'll be able to find the distance between two points on a grid and the volume and surface area of a box.
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with arithmetic, fractions and basic algebra; no earlier geometry is assumed.
